findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a manager selects a locally checked-out ready item and a ready item published by a teammate on another machine.
The new checkout resolves the earlier refusal, but it does not bring the teammate's ready receipt with it: `repo.ready_path` stores that receipt in the uncommitted shared Git directory (`src/forge/repo.py:792`). Although `nextstep._item_readiness` accepts the published PR record (`src/forge/nextstep.py:878-883`), `_form_train` still requires the local receipt (`src/forge/land.py:617-627`). With only these two items selected, the teammate's item stays out and no combined train forms; they close and merge separately, with a possible per-merge re-test. This leaves the original teammate scenario short of the required combined check.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a named-items run starts a member's checks again through GitHub's API.
The new assertion catches `gh run rerun` and `gh workflow run`, but not `gh api --method POST` to GitHub's [workflow rerun endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs#re-run-a-workflow). The fixture accepts generic API calls (`tests/test_setup.py:224`), so such a rerun can leave every assertion passing while repeating the member's check. The existing `--all` proof also checks for API POSTs (`tests/test_train_land_all.py:311-314`); the named proof still does not fully guard the previously reported no-rerun behaviour.

why: forge land --all takes every item in close, including items the owner has on hold, so a team cannot land a chosen set of Ready items with one combined check; merging them one by one re-runs the combined test after each merge (25-40 min each at a client). Owner, 18 Nov 2026: fix it and release fast.
